title: Placing a Hotel Rate Plans Property Credit on a Reservation after Arrival
content:
Where a guest has arrived and the property credit their rate plan in the Hotel Rate Plans range carries falls due to be placed on the reservation, the agency places it on the reservation's credit account so that it becomes spendable at the property. The result this entry governs is the amount of property credit placed and the last date on which it may be spent. Once the credit is placed, the guest can see it standing against the reservation and the property can take charges against it.

**Making the call.** The desk unlocks the hidden agent tool `post_arrival_credit_grant_b81202b7` and then calls it. The agent works the amount and the date out from the published terms and the records and hands them in; the tool prices nothing and judges nothing.

**Parameters.**

- `stay_reservation_id` — the internal reference number of the hotel reservation the credit is being placed on, read from the reservation record returned by the reservation lookup before this call.
- `credit_amount_usd` — how much property credit is placed on the reservation, as a positive USD amount with two decimal places, rounded half up to the cent. It is stored on the grant line exactly as handed in and is never blank.
- `credit_expiry_date` — the last calendar date on which this credit may be spent at the property, written as YYYY-MM-DD in the property's own local calendar, with no time part and never blank.

**What comes back.** A confirmation sentence in plain text. It names the reference of the grant line now standing on the folio, repeats the amount placed on the reservation as a USD figure to two decimal places, repeats the last date the credit may be spent as YYYY-MM-DD, and states the reservation's restated unspent property credit as a USD figure to two decimal places. The appearance of that sentence, with a grant reference in it, is what indicates the credit has been placed.
